Two temperature sensors, an NTC thermistor and a Pt1000, go into the same
stirred bath at the same instants and come out with two independent
calibration curves fitted against the same reference thermometer. Neither
curve is a straight line: the NTC's resistance is fit with the nonlinear
Steinhart–Hart equation, the Pt1000's with the IEC 60751 Callendar–Van Dusen
relation, and both fits turn out to be ordinary linear least squares once the
right columns are built.

This experiment is also where **self-heating** appears for the first time on
this site: both sensors are read by passing a current through them, and that
current warms the sensing element above the medium it is meant to be
measuring. Changing the excitation and watching the reading shift is a
systematic error the student creates and then measures — memorable in a way a
quoted datasheet number never is. [T2](../T2-temperature-dynamic/index.qmd)
uses the calibration curves fitted here to convert its own voltage records
into temperature, which is why the two experiments share a rig and are built
together.

## What you measure {#sec-t1-index-measure}

| Quantity | How | Where it is used later |
|---|---|---|
| Steinhart–Hart coefficients $A,B,C$ | Linear least squares of $1/T$ on $(1,\ln R,(\ln R)^3)$ over six bath points | Converts every NTC voltage in T1 and T2 to a temperature |
| Callendar–Van Dusen $R_0$ (and $A$) | Linear least squares with IEC 60751's $B$ fixed | Converts every Pt1000 voltage in T1 and T2 to a temperature |
| Sensitivity, divider vs. bridge | Symbolic derivative of each front end, evaluated at an operating point | Combined with S1's noise floor into a resolution in kelvin |
| Self-heating dissipation constant $\delta$ | Apparent temperature shift between a low- and a high-excitation reading of the same bath point | Bounds how hard either sensor can be driven without biasing the reading |

: What T1 produces {#tbl-t1-index-outputs}

## Bench {#sec-t1-index-bench}

**Tier 2.** A supported board, [the conditioning board](../../hardware/conditioning-board.qmd)
for the Pt1000's instrumentation amplifier, [the thermal rig](../../hardware/thermal-rig.qmd)
— a stirred water bath, an ice bath and a reference thermometer — and the
resistors for the NTC's divider and the Pt1000's bridge.

**Board.** Any supported board works; nothing here needs streaming at a
particular rate, only a stable analog input.

**Host.** Any host is adequate; T1 makes no timing measurement and no host
comparison, unlike S1 and S3.

## Reference data {#sec-t1-index-data}

Seven generated runs ship with the experiment, in `data/`:

| File | Contents |
|---|---|
| `cal-ice`, `cal-t20`, `cal-t35`, `cal-t50`, `cal-t65`, `cal-t80` | 200 records each at 1 kHz, both sensors on separate pins in the same run, at a fixed point and five stirred-bath points |
| `selfheat-high` | The `t50` bath point again, both sensors driven at a higher excitation |

: Reference data shipped with T1 {#tbl-t1-index-data}

::: {.callout-warning}
## The reference data is synthetic

It is produced by a seeded generator (`tools/synth/t1_temperature_static.py`)
whose parameters are plausible placeholders, not measurements — marked
`TODO (Paolo)` in `tools/synth/params/t1.yaml`, with one exception: the
Callendar–Van Dusen coefficients are the published IEC 60751 standard, not a
placeholder. The generator exists so the analysis templates render, and are
checked in continuous integration, with no bench attached. Every page that
uses it says so.
:::

::: {.content-visible when-profile="instructor"}
## Instructor summary {.instructor-note}

Four hours, tier 2, needs S1 as a prerequisite for the resolution comparison
of the [sensitivity comparison](handbook.qmd#sec-t1-sensitivity) — the two
nonlinear calibration fits and the
self-heating measurement are where the session earns its extra hour over S1.
Full notes, expected values, common failures and the rubric are in the
[handbook](handbook.qmd#sec-t1-instructor).
:::
